headline: Similar shirts worn by police officer and murder suspect raise questions
summary: Family members and locals claim a suspect in the Rangpur family murders was given a shirt by police, after a police officer was seen wearing a similar one at the crime scene.
details: Four members of a family in Rangpur's Daspara area were found murdered in their home on Saturday night. The victims include a retired teacher, his wife, and their two children.
Police arrested two suspects, Siddhartha Das and Mugdho Das, in connection with the killings. Two of the accused have since confessed to the crimes.
Controversy has emerged after a police officer, Sanatan Chakrabarty, was seen wearing a specific shirt at the crime scene on Saturday night.
Siddhartha Das was later taken to court wearing a shirt that appeared nearly identical to the one worn by the officer.
The suspect's father and brother claim Siddhartha was wearing a black vest when detained and had never owned such a shirt, suggesting police provided it.
Sanatan Chakrabarty has denied the allegations, stating that the shirt he wore is still in his possession and was purchased from Aarong.
The incident has sparked widespread discussion and skepticism on Facebook, with locals and relatives rejecting the police version of events.
caption:
A police officer and a murder suspect were seen wearing the same shirt. Now, the family of the suspect is questioning the police investigation.

Four members of a family in Rangpur's Daspara area were found murdered in their home on Saturday night. The victims include a retired teacher, his wife, and their two children.

Police arrested two suspects, Siddhartha Das and Mugdho Das, in connection with the killings. Two of the accused have since confessed to the crimes.

Controversy has emerged after a police officer, Sanatan Chakrabarty, was seen wearing a specific shirt at the crime scene on Saturday night.

Siddhartha Das was later taken to court wearing a shirt that appeared nearly identical to the one worn by the officer.

The suspect's father and brother claim Siddhartha was wearing a black vest when detained and had never owned such a shirt, suggesting police provided it.

Sanatan Chakrabarty has denied the allegations, stating that the shirt he wore is still in his possession and was purchased from Aarong.

The incident has sparked widespread discussion and skepticism on Facebook, with locals and relatives rejecting the police version of events.

headline_marked: Brazil football team [[could visit Bangladesh]] for friendly match
headline: Brazil football team could visit Bangladesh for friendly match
summary: A Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) delegation has inspected venues in Dhaka, exploring the possibility of a match against Bangladesh or using the city as a neutral venue.
details: A five-member delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) visited Dhaka on Sunday to explore the possibility of the five-time world champions visiting Bangladesh.
The delegation inspected the National Stadium, Bashundhara Kings Arena, and several hotels to assess the facilities and infrastructure.
BFF president Tabith Awal met with the delegation to discuss security, possible renovations at the National Stadium, and the potential for a friendly match in September or October.
The CBF delegation found the venues and infrastructure to be 'acceptable' but recommended improvements to dressing rooms, technical zones, and security at entry and exit gates.
The BFF stated that these recommended improvements could be completed within a short period.
The talks could focus on either Bangladesh playing an international friendly against Brazil or Brazil using Bangladesh as a neutral venue.
The CBF will submit its observations and recommendations to its board this week before further talks with the Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF).
Meanwhile, Bangladesh is scheduled to compete in the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup in Indonesia from September 24 to October 4.
caption:
Could the five-time world champions land in Dhaka? 🇧🇷🇧🇩

A five-member delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) visited Dhaka on Sunday to explore the possibility of the five-time world champions visiting Bangladesh.

The delegation inspected the National Stadium, Bashundhara Kings Arena, and several hotels to assess the facilities and infrastructure.

BFF president Tabith Awal met with the delegation to discuss security, possible renovations at the National Stadium, and the potential for a friendly match in September or October.

The CBF delegation found the venues and infrastructure to be 'acceptable' but recommended improvements to dressing rooms, technical zones, and security at entry and exit gates.

The BFF stated that these recommended improvements could be completed within a short period.

The talks could focus on either Bangladesh playing an international friendly against Brazil or Brazil using Bangladesh as a neutral venue.

The CBF will submit its observations and recommendations to its board this week before further talks with the Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF).

Meanwhile, Bangladesh is scheduled to compete in the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup in Indonesia from September 24 to October 4.
